query: You also know about this, what are the steps to have VA for PTSD?
answer: To get VA care for PTSD, you generally need to apply for VA health care first. You can apply online, by phone at 877-222-VETS (8387), by mail, or in person at a VA medical center. Once enrolled, you can request an appointment for a mental health assessment. VA offers proven PTSD treatments like cognitive processing therapy (CPT), medication, and individual or group therapy. If you're in crisis, call the Veterans Crisis Line at [PHONE] and select 1, or go to the nearest VA medical center or emergency room—eligibility for VA health care is not required for emergency crisis care. For more specific steps, contact your nearest VA medical center or call [PHONE] (TTY: [PHONE]) Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET.

query: am I eligible for VR&E benefits and services?
answer: Eligibility for VR&E benefits depends on your specific situation. Generally, you may be eligible if you are a service member or veteran with a service-connected disability and an employment handicap (your disability limits your ability to prepare for, obtain, or maintain suitable employment). Specific conditions include: if you have a VA disability rating, you can apply through eBenefits; if you're a service member without a rating, you may qualify if you're going through the Physical Evaluation Board process, expect an other than dishonorable discharge with a VA memorandum rating of 20% or more, or are in the Integrated Disability Evaluation System (IDES). Severely injured active-duty members may automatically receive benefits under certain laws. After applying, a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor will determine if you have an employment handicap and eligibility. For more precise guidance, please clarify your current status (e.g., veteran with rating, active duty, etc.).
